whenToChoose.label: You prioritize social discovery over privacy and don't mind your research being publicly visible by default
You primarily highlight web content and don't need advanced note-taking, multimedia capture, or offline capabilities
You're willing to accept reliability issues, sync problems, and limited browser support for the sake of social features
You don't require serious research tools like advanced search, semantic linking, or data portability beyond basic export

notes.offline: Glasp is entirely cloud-dependent with zero offline functionality.
notes.e2ee: No end-to-end encryption is availabile and there isn't much information available about the security of the app. [Ref](https://glasp.co/terms-of-service)
notes.bug-bounty: No structured security program or bug bounty system.
notes.data-selling: Glasp's [privacy policy](https://glasp.co/privacy-policy) states that user's personal data will be shared with Glasp's service providers. While sharing certain information like email might be essential for communication or transactional purposes, it is not clear from the policy on what personal information is shared. The policy also explicitly states that Glasp may sell user information in cases of merger/acquisition/sale. Also, the social-first design makes most content public by default, potentially exposing sensitive research or personal reading habits without clear user understanding.
notes.email-consent: Glasp does not show any explicit email consent screen during signup. However, the emails sent by Glasp has *unsubscribe* and *change email frequency* options.
notes.spam-rate: Glasp has explicit controls over the frequency of communication received from Glasp.
notes.anonymous-data-collection: No explicit consent was asked by Glasp during signup or onboarding process. However, Glasp seems to use analytics software for the improvement of the product, gathering user data and user usage information.

notes.bug-free: No public status page raises transparency concerns about service reliability. Users must rely on community reports rather than official uptime metrics, indicating less mature operational practices. [Reference](https://blog.glasp.co/glasp-youtube-summary-extension-status/)
notes.uptime: Recent technical issues reported include VPN compatibility problems and authentication bugs for highlight imports. Storage limitations can cause data loss when limits are exceeded without adequate warning.
notes.performance: While generally responsive, the extension struggles with complex web pages and single-page applications. Performance degrades on sites with heavy JavaScript or dynamic content loading.
notes.sync-reliability: Cross-device synchronization is notably unreliable. Users frequently report highlights disappearing or not syncing across browsers and devices, creating data integrity concerns for serious research use.
notes.crash-free: Regular browser extension bugs occur, particularly on modern web applications. Updates often required to maintain compatibility, suggesting unstable extension architecture.
notes.platform-stability: Limited browser support compared to competitors. Chrome-centric development means inconsistent experiences on other browsers. iOS app lacks feature parity with web extension.

notes.setup-ease: While initial setup is straightforward, users often miss privacy implications during quick registration. Default public sharing settings catch many users unaware, requiring later privacy adjustments.
notes.learning-curve: Simple highlighting interface, but understanding social implications and privacy settings requires deeper exploration. Many users accidentally create public highlights before understanding the social nature.
notes.maintenance: Frequent extension updates required to maintain functionality suggests architectural instability. Users must actively monitor for updates to prevent sync issues, adding maintenance burden compared to more stable alternatives.

notes.email-support: Support primarily through email with no guaranteed response times. No live chat or phone support options for urgent issues, limiting accessibility for business users.
notes.community-support: Community support exists but is limited in scope compared to established platforms. Smaller user base means fewer available solutions for technical issues.
notes.documentation: Documentation covers basic features but lacks depth for advanced use cases. Limited troubleshooting guides for sync issues or data recovery scenarios that users frequently encounter.

notes.business-model: Freemium model with unclear monetization strategy. Limited premium features may not sustain long-term operational costs, raising questions about service continuity. [Reference](https://idrisharuna.hashnode.dev/the-benefits-and-limitations-of-using-glasp-social-web-highlighter-for-collaborative-research)
notes.export-capabilities: While export exists, social context and community connections are lost during export, significantly reducing data value. Export formats lack preservation of highlight relationships and social interactions.
notes.self-hosting: Complete dependency on Glasp infrastructure with no self-hosting alternative creates single point of failure risks. Users have zero control over service availability or data residency.
notes.data-portability: Export functionality is basic and doesn't preserve the social graph, highlight relationships, or community interactions that make Glasp valuable. Data becomes significantly less useful when exported.
notes.financial-stability: Young company (founded 2021) with typical venture funding pressures. Unclear revenue model and user acquisition strategy raise sustainability concerns compared to established alternatives.
notes.vendor-lock-in: High vendor lock-in due to social features being core value proposition. Switching costs are high because social connections and community interactions cannot be migrated to other platforms.

notes.zero-dark-patterns:
The following dark patterns are noticed on the Glasp app.
 1. Shows paywall immediately upon signup even before the user tests the app.
notes.transparency: Glasp is not transparent about its data collection and usage practices. This is a violation of ethical design principles.

notes.editor-support: Notes interface provides basic text formatting but limited markdown support. No dedicated markdown editor or preview.
notes.syntax-support: Basic support for links and simple formatting in notes. No support for headers, lists, code blocks, or advanced markdown syntax.
notes.rendering: Notes are displayed as formatted text but without full markdown rendering capabilities.
notes.import-export: Exported notes maintain basic formatting but not full markdown compatibility.

notes.annotation-quality: Good PDF highlighting through browser extension. Highlights are preserved and can be organized. Works well with web-based PDF viewers.
notes.local-pdf-support: Supports PDFs opened in browser. Limited support for locally stored PDFs - requires opening in browser first.
notes.annotation-types: Primarily text highlighting with ability to add notes. No support for drawing, stamps, or advanced annotation types.
notes.sync-across-devices: PDF highlights sync across devices through Glasp account. Can access PDF highlights from web app and mobile.
notes.export-integration: PDF highlights included in export functionality. Can extract all PDF annotations and notes.

notes.standalone-notes: Severely limited standalone note creation capability. The platform forces users into a highlighting-first workflow that doesn't accommodate traditional note-taking needs or original thought capture.
notes.note-quality: Basic note editor lacks essential features like formatting, table support, or rich media embedding. Notes feel like afterthoughts rather than first-class content types.
notes.organization: Notes are trapped within the highlighting context, making it difficult to develop independent thoughts or create structured knowledge bases. No hierarchical note organization.
notes.search-in-notes: Search functionality is basic and doesn't provide advanced filtering or semantic search capabilities that would be expected in a research tool.

notes.highlighting-quality: While highlighting works, it often fails on modern web applications with dynamic content loading. Highlights frequently disappear when pages update or reload, creating data integrity issues.
notes.page-compatibility: Limited compatibility with single-page applications, progressive web apps, and sites with complex JavaScript. Many modern websites break the highlighting functionality entirely.
notes.context-preservation: Context preservation is inconsistent, especially on sites that update content dynamically. Original page context can become stale or broken over time.
notes.annotation-workflow: Workflow is simplistic and lacks advanced features like multi-level annotations, annotation threading, or collaborative editing that power users expect.
notes.cross-browser-support: Browser support is limited compared to competitors. Firefox users are excluded, and Safari support is incomplete with missing features.
notes.social-integration: Social features create privacy concerns as highlights become public by default. Many users are surprised to discover their research is publicly visible without explicit consent. [Reference](https://glasp.co/web-highlighter)

notes.youtube-support: YouTube support is extremely limited, only working on static text elements like descriptions. Cannot capture actual video content, timestamps, or key moments that would be useful for research or learning.
notes.video-annotation: No meaningful video annotation capabilities. Users cannot create timestamped notes, capture video frames, or annotate specific moments in videos - fundamental features for video-based learning.
notes.platform-coverage: Platform coverage is misleading - while extension works on video sites, it provides no video-specific functionality beyond basic webpage highlighting.
notes.workflow-integration: Video content is poorly integrated with highlights, creating disconnected experiences for multimedia research. No video-specific organization or playback features.

notes.platform-support: Good support for Twitter, LinkedIn, and other social platforms. Can highlight posts and comments.
notes.context-preservation: Preserves social media post context including author information and original links.
notes.community-features: Strong community aspect where users can share and discover highlights from social media. Creates learning communities around topics.
notes.privacy-considerations: Social clipping is public by default, which aligns with platform's social learning mission but may not suit private research.

notes.tagging-system: Good tagging system allows categorization during highlighting. Can add multiple tags to organize content by topic.
notes.workflow-integration: Tagging is integrated into highlighting workflow, making it easy to categorize content while reading.
notes.topic-organization: Can organize highlights into topics and collections for better content curation.
notes.curation-tools: Provides tools for organizing highlights into meaningful collections for later reference and sharing.

notes.organization-depth: Strong hierarchical organization with topics, tags, and custom collections. Multiple ways to organize content.
notes.collection-sharing: Can share collections publicly, enabling collaborative curation and knowledge sharing.
notes.discovery-features: Collections are discoverable by other users, creating learning opportunities from curated content.
notes.management-tools: Good tools for managing and reorganizing collections. Can move highlights between collections easily.

notes.search-scope: Search includes social content from followed users, creating noise in results and making it difficult to focus on personal research. No way to limit search to only personal highlights.
notes.search-quality: Basic keyword matching without semantic understanding or advanced relevance ranking. Search quality degrades significantly as highlight collections grow larger.
notes.filtering-options: Limited filtering options compared to dedicated research tools. Cannot filter by highlight color, annotation depth, or other research-specific criteria that would be valuable for serious users.
notes.performance: Search performance becomes sluggish with larger datasets. No advanced search operators or boolean logic support limits research effectiveness. [Reference](https://glasp.co/web-highlighter)

notes.connection-features: Limited explicit backlinking. Connections are mainly through shared tags and topics rather than direct linking.
notes.relationship-discovery: Can discover related content through tags and user activity but no automated relationship detection.
notes.link-visualization: No visual representation of connections between highlights or concepts.
notes.knowledge-graph: No knowledge graph features or concept mapping. Relationships are implicit through tagging system.
